items.title: Welcome
items.text:
Ryokan is a self-hosted anime PVR inspired by Sonarr.

It's made around how anime is released: fansub groups, batch packs, SeaDex picks, AniList for metadata, and auto search that just works.

Project status

Ryokan is a one-person vibecoded project, so expect some rough edges.

items.title: Get started
items.text:
Ryokan runs as a Docker container. These docs assume you know what containers, images and volumes are.

Start with the Quick start

The Quick start lets you build a docker-compose.yml for Ryokan, your download client, a media server, and optionally Seerr and a reverse proxy. It then walks you through setting each one up.

Guides:

  1. Quick start: from installing Docker to a first episode.
  2. Docker installation: setting up a basic install of Ryokan.
  3. Configuration: what each Settings tab does.
  4. Download clients: setup notes for each client.
  5. External accounts: linking AniList/MAL.

items.text:
• Troubleshooting: common problems and how to fix them.
  • FAQ: how Ryokan compares to Sonarr, multiple users, API access, and other questions.

items.title: Calendar
items.text: The Calendar page shows when episodes air for the shows in your library. You can also subscribe to it from Apple Calendar, Google Calendar or Thunderbird.

items.title: Views
items.text:
• This week: a list, grouped by day, with today highlighted.
  • Next week: the same for the seven days after.
  • This month: a month grid.

items.title: What each episode shows
items.text:
• The series cover and title.
  • The episode number. Each season is its own series in Ryokan, so the first episode of Re:Zero 4th Season is E01, not S04E01.
  • A Premiere badge in the list, or a ★ in the grid, on the first episode of a series.
  • Whether the series is Monitored.

Click an episode to open its series page.

items.title: Filtering
items.text:
• Search matches romaji, English and native titles, so "attack on titan" finds Shingeki no Kyojin.
  • Monitored only hides series that are not monitored.

items.title: Subscribing from your calendar app
items.text:
1. Create an API key with the calendar scope under Settings → API Keys, if you do not have one.
  2. On the Calendar page, click iCal Link, choose the key, and copy the URL.
  3. Add the URL to your calendar app:
    • Apple Calendar: File → New Calendar Subscription
    • Google Calendar: Other calendars → + → From URL
    • Thunderbird: New Calendar → On the Network → iCalendar (ICS)

The URL contains the key, so treat it like a password.

The feed covers the next 30 days. To change that, add options to the end of the URL:

  • &days=N sets the number of days, up to 90.
  • &monitored=true leaves out series that are not monitored.

items.title: How current the times are
items.text:
Air times come from AniList. Ryokan fetches them when you add a series and refreshes them every 12 hours.

To refresh now, go to System → Scheduled Tasks and click Run now on Episode air-date refresh.

items.title: Series added from MyAnimeList
items.text:
A series that AniList has no entry for, which Ryokan added from MyAnimeList instead, does not appear on the calendar. This mostly affects old or obscure titles.

Last updated: 2026-10-04.

items.title: Configuration
items.text: This page describes each tab under Settings. Changes take effect when you save. Nothing needs a restart.

items.title: Connections
items.text:
Other services Ryokan talks to.

  • AniList / MyAnimeList: link an account and shows on your watch list are added to the library. See External accounts.
  • Sync interval (minutes): how often the watch list is checked. Default 30, minimum 15, maximum 10080 (7 days).
  • Media Server: your Jellyfin, Emby or Plex server. Pick the Type, then enter its URL and API key. Ryokan asks the server to refresh its library after each import. For Jellyfin the URL is http://jellyfin:8096 when both run in the same compose file. Otherwise use the address you open the server with in a browser. Emby keys are under API Keys in its server settings. For Plex, paste your X-Plex-Token in the API key field. Ryokan connects to one media server at a time.
  • Sonarr / Radarr API: lets Seerr and similar tools request anime from Ryokan as if it were Sonarr or Radarr. The Sonarr API is at /api/v3/, the Radarr API at /radarr/api/v3/, and each has its own key.

items.title: Saved passwords and keys
items.text:
Ryokan never shows a saved password or key again. The field reads [set; leave blank to keep].

  • Leave it blank to keep the saved value.
  • Type a new value to replace it.
  • Press Clear to remove it.

If you change a service's address (host, port, or http to https), type the password or key again. Ryokan will not send a saved secret to a new address.

For a webhook, a saved header shows its name with ******** in place of the value, and a saved URL shows only its host.

items.title: Download Clients
items.text:
Add one or more of qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission, rTorrent and SABnzbd. Setup notes for each are on the Download clients page.

There is one Default client for torrents and one for Usenet. Grabs from Nyaa and torznab indexers go to the torrent default, and grabs from newznab indexers go to the Usenet default.

items.title: Indexers
items.text:
An indexer is a place Ryokan searches. Nyaa is built in and is the first card. Add torznab and newznab indexers (usually through Prowlarr or Jackett) and direct RSS feeds, such as SubsPlease, here.

Each indexer has two optional fields:

  • Categories: leave blank and Ryokan asks for Anime (5070), plus Movies (2000) for a film and XXX (6000) for an adult title. If the indexer offers none of those, Ryokan asks for the categories it does offer. The RSS poll asks for every category your library needs. If you fill the field in, those category ids are sent on every search and RSS poll, comma separated. The edit form lists the categories the indexer offers. Click one to add or remove it.
  • Download client: sends this indexer's grabs to a specific client, overriding the default. Use it when one tracker needs a client with its own seeding rules.

items.title: Nyaa
items.text:
The Nyaa card cannot be removed, but you can click it to:

  • turn it off. Automatic and interactive searches then skip Nyaa and its RSS feed stops. The Search page keeps working.
  • turn its RSS feed on or off
  • choose between English-translated releases and all anime for automatic grabs
  • send its grabs to a specific torrent client
  • restrict searches to one uploader. A series can override this on its own page.

items.title: autobrr webhook
items.text:
autobrr watches tracker announce channels and can push new releases to Ryokan at /api/webhook/autobrr. The webhook has its own API key, shown on this tab.

Name the indexer in Ryokan the same as autobrr's identifier for it, such as animebytes. A push from that indexer then uses its download client and seed rules. A push from nyaa uses the Nyaa card's client.

A torrent push from an indexer Ryokan does not know is still grabbed, through the default torrent client and without seed rules. A push that is not a torrent, such as a Usenet release, is skipped.

items.title: Quality & Releases
items.text:
These settings decide which release wins when several match an episode. How releases are scored explains how they combine.

  • Preferred / blocked groups: releases from preferred groups score higher. Releases from blocked groups are never grabbed.
  • Preferred resolution / source: releases below the resolution, or from the wrong source, are filtered out before scoring.
  • Cutoff source / resolution: once an episode has a file at or above the cutoff, Ryokan stops looking for a better one.
  • Finished-series quality: a second cutoff that applies once AniList marks the series as finished. A common setup is WEB while a show airs and BluRay afterwards.
  • Propers and Repacks: what to do with a v2, PROPER or REPACK of a release you already have. See Replacing a file you already have.
    • Prefer and upgrade (default): scores it higher, and replaces your file when it comes from the same group.
    • Prefer, do not upgrade: scores it higher only.
    • Do not prefer: ignores revisions.
  • Upgrade Until Custom Format Score: a file that already meets the quality cutoff is still replaced by a release of the same quality with a higher Custom Format score, until the file's score reaches this number. The default, 0, turns this off for any file scoring 0 or more.
  • Minimum Custom Format Score Increment: how much higher the new release has to score for that kind of upgrade. Default 1.
  • Audio preference: subtitled, dubbed, or no preference. It changes scores but does not filter anything out.
  • SeaDex enabled: gives a large score bonus to the releases SeaDex recommends. If you add a Custom Format that uses SeaDexBest, the Custom Format is used and this switch is ignored.
  • Default custom query tokens: words added to every search, such as bd 1080p. A series can override them on its own page.

items.title: Custom Formats
items.text:
Custom Formats are Sonarr-style scoring rules. Each release is checked against every Custom Format and the matching scores are added up.

  • Custom Formats list: add, edit and delete formats. Paste a release title into the test box to see which formats match and the total score. Install Defaults loads a set made for anime.
  • Minimum Score: automatic searches ignore releases that score below this. They still appear in interactive search.
  • Import / Export: Ryokan reads and writes Sonarr v4 Custom Format JSON, so you can paste formats from TRaSH-Guides or from Sonarr.

items.title: Release Groups
items.text:
A table of what each release group usually releases, for example that VCB-Studio releases are BluRay encodes. Ryokan uses it when a file name does not say whether the release is BluRay or WEB.

The table comes filled in. The tab also lists Suggested Mappings you can accept or edit. Rows you add win over the built-in ones.

items.title: API Keys
items.text:
Keys for other tools that connect to Ryokan. Each key has a name and one or more scopes, which decide what it may do. The key is shown once, when you create it.

  • calendar: read the calendar subscription feed. The Calendar page builds the subscription URL for you.
  • admin: everything.
  • search, library:read, library:write: not used yet.

items.title: Library and imports
items.text:
• Media Root Path: where imported episodes go. This is the path inside Ryokan's container. In the quick start, /media/anime is /srv/media/anime on the host.
  • Enable post-processing: rename finished downloads, place them in the library, and write NFO files for Jellyfin. Needs a media root and a download client.
  • File operation mode:
    • hardlink (default): the library file and the download are the same data on disk, so the torrent keeps seeding and no extra space is used. Falls back to a copy when the two folders are on different filesystems.
    • copy
    • move

  • Import subtitle files: off by default. When on, subtitle files that come with a download are placed next to the episode and named after it, with the language from the subtitle's own name, for example Show - S01E05 - Title.en.ass. Deleting or replacing the episode removes them too. Subtitle file extensions sets which files count (srt and ass by default).

    A subtitle belongs to a video when one of these is true:

    • its name starts with the video's name
    • it has the same episode number
    • its folder is named after the video, as in a pack's Subs/ layout

    If none of those match and the download has only one video, every subtitle goes to that episode. When a download has several subtitles of the same kind, they are numbered.

  • Give up on stuck imports after (hours): if a download has finished but Ryokan cannot find a video file to import after this long, the download is marked failed, you are notified, and the release goes on the blocklist under Downloads → Blocklist. Remove it from there to allow it to be grabbed again. Default 24. 0 never gives up. The usual cause is that Ryokan cannot see the download folder. Nothing is given up on in the first 15 minutes after a restart, so a download folder that mounts late is not mistaken for a stuck import.

  • Preferred Title Language: romaji, english or native. Sets the title shown in the UI and used by the {series.title} naming token. Searches match all three whichever you pick.

items.title: File naming
items.text:
Three templates set where an import goes:

Template Default Applies Series folder {series.title} once, when the series is added Season folder Season {season.number:00} on every import Episode file {series.title} - S{season.number:00}E{episode.number:00} - {episode.title}{ext} on every import

Each field shows a sample as you type, and Reset restores the default. Changing a template never renames folders or files already in the library.

The episode template must include {episode.number} and end with {ext}. Ryokan refuses a template if it cannot read the episode number back out of the sample name, because scans and upgrades rely on that.

Token Renders {series.title} Series title in your preferred title language {series.year} Premiere year {season.number} Season number, currently always 1. {season.number:00} pads to 01 {episode.number} Episode number. :00 pads to 01, :000 to 001 {episode.absolute} Episode number counted across all seasons, as fansub groups number sequels: 019 for episode 7 of a second season that follows 12 episodes. :000 pads {episode.title} Episode title {quality.full} Resolution and source, like 1080p WEB-DL {quality.resolution} 1080p, 720p, ... {quality.source} BluRay, BluRay Remux, WEB-DL, WEBRip, DVD, HDTV {group} Release group {ext} File extension, including the dot

Things to know:

  • A token with no value is left out along with its brackets or separator, so [{group}] never leaves an empty [].
  • {episode.absolute} is empty for specials, and for a sequel until Ryokan has refreshed its metadata once. Put it after the episode number, as in S01E07 - 019, so scans read the right number.
  • A file holding several episodes is named with the range: S01E05-E06, or 05-06 after a dash.
  • Characters that file names cannot contain (/ \ : * ? " < > |) become _.
  • A name that is too long for the filesystem is shortened at the series title. The episode number and extension are always kept.
  • On Windows, a warning appears when the sample path is longer than 260 characters.
  • Quality and group come from the release that was grabbed. A manual quality override on an episode is used instead.

items.title: Backups
items.text:
• Scheduled backups: off by default. Daily or weekly, Ryokan saves its database and encryption key, and cached artwork if you tick it, to the backup folder. Manual backups and restores are under System → Backup.
  • Backup folder: a path inside Ryokan's container. Empty means a backups folder next to the database (/data/backups in Docker). A folder on another disk is safer.
  • Backups to keep: older scheduled backups are deleted after each new one. Default 7. Backups taken automatically before a restore are never deleted.

Note

Copying ryokan.db yourself while Ryokan is running can miss recent changes. The built-in backup does not have that problem.

items.title: Recycle bin
items.text:
• Recycle bin path: empty by default, which makes deletes permanent. Set a folder (a path inside the container) and deleted episodes, removed series, and files replaced by an upgrade are moved there instead. Restore or delete them for good from the Recycle Bin on the Library page.
  • Purge after (days): recycled items older than this are deleted. Default 14. 0 keeps them until you empty the bin.

Things to know:

  • Put the bin on the same filesystem as the media root. The move is then instant and keeps hardlinks to seeding torrents.
  • If Ryokan cannot write to the path, deletes are refused until you fix or clear it.
  • Restoring puts the files back. It does not re-add a torrent that was removed from the download client.

items.title: Searching and grabbing
items.text:
• Enable automatic RSS sync: check RSS feeds on a schedule and grab matching releases. Each indexer also has its own RSS switch on the Indexers tab.
  • RSS Sync Interval (minutes): default 15, minimum 1, maximum 60.
  • Search for monitored episodes when a series is added: on by default.
  • Search when monitoring is widened: search for episodes that become monitored when you change a series' monitoring, for example from none to all. Off by default.
  • Add the series to the library when grabbing from Search: on by default. When off, a grab from the Search page goes to the download client and Ryokan does not track the series.
  • Interactive file picker: Batches only (default) opens the file picker when you grab a multi-file torrent. Never grabs everything with one click. Usenet releases always download whole.

items.title: Failed downloads
items.text:
• Remove and blocklist detected misgrabs: on by default. When the files in a download clearly belong to a different series, Ryokan removes the download, blocklists the release, notifies you and searches again. When off, the download stays in the client, is not imported, and is listed under System → Misgrabs.
  • Search again after a failed download: on by default. When the download client reports a download as failed, Ryokan blocklists the release, removes the download, notifies you and searches for another. It stops after three failures for one series in a day.

A download the client only flags with a warning, such as qBittorrent's "missing files", is left alone and stays on the Downloads page.

Nothing is marked failed in the first 15 minutes after a restart.

A failed import is not retried either. The download itself is fine, so downloading it again would not help. Check the logs for what went wrong.

Each download client has a Remove failed downloads box (on by default) that decides whether a failed download is also removed from that client.

items.title: Reset or wipe
items.text:
• Remove one series: use Remove from Library on its page. You can delete its files at the same time.
  • Wipe everything: stop Ryokan, delete its data folder (/srv/docker/ryokan in the quick start), and start it again. First-run setup runs again.
  • Forgot your password: see Reset auth. Your library and linked accounts are kept.

The Force MAL / Kitsu fallback switches are on the System page, under Debug.

Last updated: 2026-10-04.

items.title: Docker reference
items.text: Environment variables, volumes, updating, and a few less common setups. For a step-by-step install, see Docker installation.

items.title: Environment variables
items.text:
Most installs only set PUID, PGID and TZ.

Variable Default Purpose PUID / PGID 1000 / 1000 The user and group Ryokan runs as. See PUID and PGID. TZ UTC Timezone for times in the UI and logs, such as America/Chicago or Europe/London. LISTEN_ADDR 0.0.0.0:8978 Address and port Ryokan listens on. RUST_LOG ryokan=info What is printed to the container log. ryokan=debug prints more. RYOKAN_DB_LOG_LEVEL info The log level for System → Logs: trace, debug, info, warn or error. Trace is the most verbose while error is the least verbose. RYOKAN_DATA_DIR /data The folder for Ryokan's own files. See Moving Ryokan's data folder. RYOKAN_TRUSTED_PROXY off Set to 1 behind a reverse proxy. See Running behind a reverse proxy. RYOKAN_COOKIE_SECURE off Forces the Secure flag on the login cookie. Only needed for an HTTPS proxy that does not send X-Forwarded-Proto. With this set you cannot stay logged in over plain HTTP. RYOKAN_FRAME_ANCESTORS any site Which pages may show Ryokan inside a frame: self, none, or one or more origins like https://dash.example.com, separated by spaces or commas. Leave it unset, or list your dashboard, if you embed Ryokan in Organizr or Homarr. RYOKAN_HOST_CHECK off Set to 1 to turn on the host check. Ryokan's pages will then only answer to an IP address, localhost, or a name listed in RYOKAN_ALLOWED_HOSTS. RYOKAN_ALLOWED_HOSTS unset The names you open Ryokan by, for the host check, separated by spaces or commas: nas ryokan.lan *.example.com. Leave out http:// and the port. Setting this turns the host check on, even without RYOKAN_HOST_CHECK. RYOKAN_RESET_AUTH unset Used to reset a forgotten password. See Reset auth. RYOKAN_ENCRYPTION_KEY unset A base64-encoded 32-byte key used to encrypt linked account tokens. When unset, Ryokan generates one and stores it in the data folder. Changing the key will force you to link your accounts again.

These override where single files and folders are kept. Most installs should leave them unset and use RYOKAN_DATA_DIR.

Variable Default DATABASE_URL <data folder>/ryokan.db RYOKAN_KEY_FILE_PATH <data folder>/.ryokan-key RYOKAN_ANIBRIDGE_CACHE_DIR <data folder>/cache/anibridge RYOKAN_MEDIA_CACHE_DIR <data folder>/cache/artwork

items.title: Volume layout
items.text:
volumes:
  - /srv/docker/ryokan:/config         # Ryokan's own files
  - /srv/media:/srv/media              # downloads and library
environment:
  RYOKAN_DATA_DIR: /config

This is the layout the Quick start generates.

/config holds the database, the encryption key, caches and backups. If you lose it you lose your library, history and linked accounts. RYOKAN_DATA_DIR tells Ryokan to keep its files there. Without it, Ryokan uses /data.

/srv/media is one folder that holds both your downloads and your library, for example /srv/media/downloads and /srv/media/anime. Ryokan starts without it but cannot import anything. Mount the same folder at the same path in your download client, so both see a finished file at the same place.

One folder for both matters because a hardlink only works inside a single mount. With hardlinks, an imported episode takes no extra space and the torrent keeps seeding.

items.title: Separate downloads and library folders
items.text:
volumes:
  - ryokan-data:/data
  - /srv/downloads:/downloads
  - /srv/media/anime:/media/anime

This works, but Ryokan cannot hardlink between two mounts, even when both folders are on the same disk. It copies each file instead, so an episode takes its space twice for as long as the download stays in the client. If that's what you want, set the file operation mode to Copy or Move under Settings → General.

items.title: Moving Ryokan's data folder
items.text:
An install that keeps Ryokan's files in /data can move them, to free /data for a shared media folder or to match the layout above. The container takes ownership of the folder RYOKAN_DATA_DIR names and leaves every other mount alone.

To move an existing install:

  1. Stop Ryokan.
  2. Copy everything from the old data volume to the new one, including the hidden .ryokan-key file. Without it you have to link your AniList and MyAnimeList accounts again.
  3. If your compose file sets DATABASE_URL, RYOKAN_KEY_FILE_PATH, RYOKAN_MEDIA_CACHE_DIR or RYOKAN_ANIBRIDGE_CACHE_DIR, remove them. They would keep pointing at the old location.
  4. Set RYOKAN_DATA_DIR, change the volume line, and start Ryokan.
  5. If Settings → General → Backup folder points into the old data folder, such as /data/backups, clear it.

items.title: Healthcheck
items.text: The image checks itself by requesting /login every 30 seconds, and docker ps shows the result as healthy or unhealthy.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Do not run docker compose down -v

-v deletes named volumes, which means your database, encryption key and library. It cannot be undone. docker compose down without -v is safe.

items.title: Branch and pull request images
items.text:
Every branch pushed to the repository is published as an image tagged with the branch name, with / replaced by -. For the example branch feat/hello-bro:

docker pull ghcr.io/johnthreekay/ryokan:feat-hello-bro

Pull requests from forks cannot publish images. Their build is attached to the pull request's Publish Docker image run under Actions, as ryokan-pr-<number>-linux-amd64 or -linux-arm64, and is kept for 14 days. Download it and load it:

docker load -i ryokan-pr-123-linux-amd64.tar
docker run -p 8978:8978 -v ./data:/data ghcr.io/johnthreekay/ryokan:pr-123

items.title: Reset auth
items.text:
If you forget your password, you can delete the account and create a new one. Your library, settings and linked accounts are kept.

  1. Add RYOKAN_RESET_AUTH=1 to the environment section of your compose file.

  2. Create an empty file named .reset-auth next to ryokan.db:

    docker exec ryokan touch /data/.reset-auth

    Use your RYOKAN_DATA_DIR in place of /data if you changed it.

  3. Start Ryokan again from the folder that holds your compose file:

    docker compose up -d

    This recreates the container with the new variable. You can optionally use --force-recreate to be absolutely certain the container is recreated.

  4. Open Ryokan. It asks you to create a new account.

  5. Remove RYOKAN_RESET_AUTH from the compose file and run docker compose up -d once more.

Both the variable and the file are required, so that a variable left in the compose file cannot delete your account on every restart.

items.title: Host check
items.text:
The host check makes the web UI answer only when it is opened by an IP address, by localhost, or by a name you have listed. It is off by default.

It protects against DNS rebinding, where a web page on another site points its own name at your Ryokan's address and then acts as if it were Ryokan's own page.

items.title: Turning it on
items.text:
1. Work out every name you open Ryokan by. Look at the address bar on each device you use: http://nas:8978 means nas, and https://ryokan.example.com means ryokan.example.com. IP addresses and localhost always work and do not need listing.

  2. Add the names to the environment section of your compose file:

    environment:
  - RYOKAN_HOST_CHECK=1
  - RYOKAN_ALLOWED_HOSTS=nas ryokan.lan ryokan.example.com

    Separate the names with spaces or commas. Leave out http:// and the port. *.example.com covers every name under example.com.

  3. Apply the change from the folder that holds your compose file:

    docker compose up -d

  4. Open Ryokan by each of the names. A name you forgot gets a "421" error page instead of Ryokan. If that happens, open Ryokan by its IP address, which always works, add the name to the list, and run docker compose up -d again.

If you only ever open Ryokan by IP address or localhost, set RYOKAN_HOST_CHECK=1 on its own and leave RYOKAN_ALLOWED_HOSTS out.

To turn the check off, remove both lines and run docker compose up -d.

items.title: Things to know
items.text:
• Ryokan also accepts the name of the machine it runs on. Inside Docker that is the container's name, which is a random ID unless your compose file sets hostname:. So your server's name still has to be listed.
  • Behind a reverse proxy with RYOKAN_TRUSTED_PROXY=1, the name the proxy uses to reach Ryokan has to be listed as well, unless the proxy passes the original host through (nginx: proxy_set_header Host $host;).
  • Seerr, autobrr and calendar apps are not affected. They use an API key and can keep calling Ryokan by its service name.

items.title: Running behind a reverse proxy
items.text:
Set RYOKAN_TRUSTED_PROXY=1. Ryokan then reads the visitor's address from X-Forwarded-For, which the login rate limit needs, and marks the login cookie Secure when the proxy reports HTTPS.

Only set it behind a proxy that overwrites X-Forwarded-For itself. If the proxy passes along whatever the visitor sent, anyone can fake their address and get around the login rate limit.

The Quick start can add a proxy to your stack. Caddy works once you put your domain in. Traefik needs three labels added to Ryokan's service, and nginx needs a config you write yourself. The generated file has a starting point for each.

Last updated: 2026-11-18.

items.title: Download clients
items.text:
Ryokan works with qBittorrent, Deluge, Transmission, rTorrent and SABnzbd. You can add more than one.

The quick start sets up a client together with Ryokan. This page is for connecting a client you already run, and for working out why a connection fails.

items.title: Setting up each client
items.text:
Clients are added under Settings → Download Clients → Add download client.

The URLs below use the service name from a compose file, such as http://qbittorrent:8080. That works when Ryokan and the client are in the same compose file. Otherwise use the address you open the client with in a browser.

Give Ryokan its own category or label, such as ryokan-anime. Ryokan only looks at downloads with that category, so it leaves everything else in the client alone.

qBittorrentDelugeTransmissionrTorrentSABnzbd

Works with qBittorrent 4.x and 5.x.

  • Kind: qBittorrent
  • URL: http://qbittorrent:8080
  • Username / Password: your web UI login
  • Category: ryokan-anime

If a grab never appears in qBittorrent

qBittorrent fetches the .torrent file itself and reports success to Ryokan before it has done so. If the fetch fails, the grab looks fine in Ryokan and is missing from qBittorrent. Check qBittorrent's log: docker compose logs qbittorrent | tail -50.

If Test connection says "Unauthorized" with the right password, look at Tools → Options → Web UI → Server domains in qBittorrent. It has to be * or include the name in Ryokan's URL.

Set a web UI password first. The default is deluge.

  • Kind: Deluge
  • URL: http://deluge:8112
  • Password: the web UI password
  • Label: ryokan-anime

Ryokan turns on Deluge's Label plugin the first time it connects. If Test connection fails with "Unknown method", click it again.

Two-step connect

Logging in to Deluge's web UI does not connect it to the Deluge daemon. That is a second step, and until it happens every request fails with "Unknown method". Ryokan does both steps when you click Test connection. If the errors come back later, the daemon has probably restarted. Click Test connection again.

Set a username and password. The linuxserver image takes them from the USER and PASS environment variables. Without them, anyone who can reach Transmission can control it.

  • Kind: Transmission
  • URL: http://transmission:9091
  • Username / Password: your USER and PASS
  • Label: ryokan-anime

Labels need Transmission 4.x. On 3.x and earlier, Ryokan tells its torrents apart by their save folder instead.

Session IDs

Transmission requires a session ID with every request and issues a new one when it restarts. Ryokan fetches it and retries by itself, so a restart of Transmission needs nothing from you.

Use the crazymax/rtorrent-rutorrent image. Set a password first: the Quick start shows the command when you pick rTorrent.

  • Kind: rTorrent
  • URL: http://rutorrent:8000/RPC2
  • Username / Password: the login from rpc.htpasswd. Leave both blank if you did not set one.
  • Label: ryokan-anime

Give each torrent its own folder

When Ryokan removes a torrent from rTorrent it also deletes the torrent's files, because rTorrent does not. If rTorrent saves every torrent straight into one shared folder, check that setup before you let Ryokan remove downloads.

A magnet link without trackers can take up to a minute to start in rTorrent.

  1. Copy the API key from Config → General → Security. Use the full API key, not the NZB key.

  2. Add sabnzbd, or whatever name is in Ryokan's URL, to Config → Special → host_whitelist. Save and restart SABnzbd. Without this, Test connection fails with a 403.

  3. Kind: SABnzbd

  4. URL: http://sabnzbd:8080. This is SABnzbd's own port, not the host port you may have mapped it to.
  5. API Key: the full API key
  6. Category: ryokan-anime. Ryokan creates it in SABnzbd when you click Test connection.

SABnzbd always downloads a whole release. Ryokan then imports the files it wants and ignores the rest.

If downloads disappear from Ryokan but are still running in SABnzbd, see Troubleshooting.

items.title: If "Test connection" fails
items.text:
• Cannot connect: a URL with a service name only works inside the same compose file. Try the client's IP address and published port.
  • Wrong port: inside a compose file, use the client's own port (SABnzbd's 8080), not the host port you mapped it to (8081 in the quick start).
  • qBittorrent says Unauthorized: see the qBittorrent tab above.
  • SABnzbd says Unauthorized: you pasted the NZB key. Use the full API key.
  • SABnzbd returns 403: the name in Ryokan's URL is not in host_whitelist.

items.title: Seeding rules and removal after import
Seeding rules
items.text:
An indexer can have a Seed Ratio and a Seed Time (minutes). Ryokan passes them to the download client with each grab from that indexer. What happens next depends on the client:

Client Seed Ratio Seed Time qBittorrent Per-torrent ratio limit Per-torrent seeding time limit Transmission Per-torrent ratio limit Idle limit: the torrent stops after that many minutes without uploading Deluge Per-torrent stop ratio Ignored rTorrent Ignored Ignored SABnzbd Not applicable Not applicable

For qBittorrent, a rule you leave empty uses qBittorrent's global limit. Before Ryokan 1.9.3, an empty rule turned that limit off for the torrent. For rTorrent, set up a ratio group in .rtorrent.rc instead.

A torrent with seeding rules is left in the client when you delete or upgrade its episode in Ryokan, so it can finish seeding.

items.title: Removing downloads
items.text:
Each client has two boxes, both on by default:

  • Remove completed downloads: once a download has been imported and the client reports it has finished seeding, Ryokan removes it from the client along with its files. Your library keeps its own copy. Usenet downloads, and torrents imported in Move mode, are removed straight after import.
  • Remove failed downloads: when the client reports a download as failed, Ryokan removes it before searching for a replacement. With the box off, the failed download stays in the client. The release is blocklisted either way.

Downloads that were only partly imported, and torrents you paused yourself, are never removed.

Let Ryokan do the removing

The client has to keep a finished download until Ryokan has imported it. Set torrent clients to pause or stop at their limit, not to delete, and set SABnzbd to keep completed jobs in its history. If the client removes a download first, Ryokan never sees it finish.

items.title: Per-client download paths
items.text:
Fill in a client's Download path when Ryokan and the client see the download folder at different paths. For example:

  • the client saves to /data/torrents, but Ryokan has the same folder mounted at /downloads
  • the client runs on a seedbox that you have mounted locally

Ryokan replaces the start of each path the client reports with this value.

Leave it empty when both use the same path, as in the quick start.

items.title: Routing: which client gets each grab
items.text:
With more than one client, Ryokan chooses in this order:

  1. The client set on the indexer, if any.
  2. For Nyaa, the client set on the Nyaa card.
  3. The default client for the type of download: the torrent default for torznab indexers and Nyaa, the Usenet default for newznab indexers.

The download keeps the client it was sent to, so changing a default later does not affect downloads already running.

Last updated: 2026-09-06.

items.title: External accounts
items.text:
Link your AniList or MyAnimeList account and Ryokan adds the anime on your lists to your library, and keeps up with changes you make there.

Accounts are linked under Settings → Connections.

items.title: Linking AniList
items.text:
1. In Ryokan, go to Settings → Connections and click Link AniList.
  2. AniList opens in a new tab. Sign in if you need to, then click Approve.
  3. Return to Ryokan. The account is linked and you can close the AniList tab.

If the new tab was blocked, allow pop-ups for Ryokan and click Link AniList again. If the tab opened but Ryokan still shows the linking box, copy the token and state from the page AniList sent you to and paste them into that box.

An AniList link lasts about a year. After that Ryokan asks you to link again.

items.title: Linking MyAnimeList
items.text:
The steps are the same: click Link MyAnimeList, approve, and return to Ryokan.

A MyAnimeList link renews itself. You only have to link again if you remove Ryokan from your MyAnimeList apps or change your MyAnimeList password.

items.title: Watch-list sync
items.text:
Ryokan checks the linked account every 30 minutes. Change that with Sync interval (minutes). The minimum is 15.

Tick the lists you want synced: Watching, Planning, Paused, Dropped, Completed. On each check, Ryokan adds series that are new on those lists and updates monitoring for series whose status changed. About once a week it reads the whole list again, which is when it notices anime you removed.

Sync now runs a check immediately.

items.title: Keeping a removed series off the sync
items.text:
Removing a series from Ryokan does not remove it from your AniList or MyAnimeList list, so the next sync adds it back.

To prevent that, tick Keep it off my … sync when you remove the series. It goes on the Sync exclusions list under Settings → Connections, and syncs skip it until you press Allow again there.

items.title: One account at a time
items.text:
Only one account can be linked at a time. While it is linked, your score for each series is shown on its library card.

Unlink removes the link and the scores that came from it. The series it added stay in your library.

items.title: Common issues
items.text:
• Re-link required: the link has expired or been revoked. Click Link again.
  • Syncs seem stalled: AniList limits how many requests Ryokan may make each minute. See Troubleshooting.
  • Linking fails right after you paste the token: linking counts against the same AniList limit. Wait a minute and try again. See Troubleshooting.
  • One MyAnimeList entry covers several series: AniList sometimes splits one MyAnimeList entry into parts, such as the stages of Steel Ball Run. A status change on MyAnimeList applies to every part in your library. The sync does not add parts you do not have.

Last updated: 2026-10-26.

items.title: How is this different from Sonarr?
items.text:
Sonarr is built for TV in general and supports anime as a special case. Ryokan only does anime. In practice:

  • Batches. Ryokan searches for a season pack with one search. Sonarr's anime mode searches every episode separately.
  • Release names. Ryokan reads fansub and BluRay-pack naming, absolute episode numbers and revisions (v2) by default.
  • Metadata. Ryokan uses AniList, so seasons and titles match how anime is listed.
  • SeaDex. Ryokan can prefer the releases SeaDex recommends.
  • BluRay or WEB. Ryokan looks at more than the release title to tell them apart, including the release group, the file itself, and whether the show is still airing.

items.title: Is this a fork of Sonarr?
items.text: No. Ryokan is written from scratch in Rust. It follows some Sonarr conventions on purpose, so that TRaSH-Guides Custom Formats and Seerr work with it.

items.title: Can it manage manga, light novels, or webtoons?
items.text: No, only anime. They may come later.

items.title: Can I run multiple Ryokan instances?
items.text:
Yes, but they know nothing about each other. Each has its own database and library. If two use the same AniList account, they share its rate limit and will hit it. See Troubleshooting.

To use one library from several machines, run one instance and reach it over your network.

items.title: Is Ryokan multi-user?
items.text: No, and there are no plans for it. Ryokan has one account. To share your library with other people, use Jellyfin, which has its own users, watch progress and parental controls.

items.title: Can I use the API directly?
items.text:
Yes. The API documentation is at /api-docs, and the OpenAPI file at /api-docs/openapi.json. Both need you to be logged in.

There are three ways to authenticate:

  • Your login session, for the same endpoints the web UI uses.
  • The Sonarr / Radarr API keys from Settings → Connections, for the endpoints Seerr calls. Send the key in the X-Api-Key header or as ?apikey=.
  • Keys from Settings → API Keys, for specific features. Currently that is the calendar feed at /api/calendar.ics. See Calendar.

items.title: Does Ryokan handle a file that holds two episodes?
items.text:
Yes. A release like Title - 05-06 or S01E05-E06 is imported as one file named with the range, and both episodes count as present. Deleting the file removes both.

Such a file is only replaced by a release that covers both episodes.

items.title: Where do OVAs and specials go?
items.text:
A special that comes inside a batch for a TV series, such as Show - OVA 01 or Show - SP1, goes into a Specials folder in the series folder and is named S00E01 style. Jellyfin, Plex and Kodi all recognise that. It does not appear in the episode list.

Automatic search and RSS do not grab specials for a TV series. Use interactive search when you want one.

A series that is itself an OVA on AniList is treated like any other series.

items.title: Can a .strm file stand in for an episode?
items.text:
Yes. A .strm file is a small text file containing a link to a stream, which Jellyfin, Emby and Kodi play in place of a video. Ryokan counts a .strm in the series folder as that episode, so the episode shows as present and is not searched for. Import Library picks them up too.

Ryokan never opens the link. The series page shows Stream link where the file size would be.

An upgrade replaces a .strm like any other file. To prevent that, turn off Upgrades on the series page.

items.title: How do I back up?
items.text:
Use System → Backup. You can download a backup, save one to a folder, schedule them, and restore from one.

To back up the files yourself, stop Ryokan first and copy the whole data folder: /srv/docker/ryokan in the quick start, or the Docker volume otherwise. A copy taken while Ryokan is running can miss recent changes.

The data folder contains a hidden .ryokan-key file. Keep it with the database. Without it you have to link your AniList and MyAnimeList accounts again.

Last updated: 2026-08-29.

items.title: Build from source
items.text: You don't need this if you run the Docker image. This page is for contributing to Ryokan or running pre-release commits from the dev branch.

items.title: What you need
items.text:
• Rust 1.95 or later.
  • A C/C++ compiler and cmake. Two of Ryokan's dependencies build native code (the TLS library and SQLite).
  • cargo-nextest (optional) for the cargo t test shortcut. Plain cargo test works without it.

items.title: Install the toolchain
items.text:
Debian or Ubuntu:

sudo apt install build-essential cmake

Fedora:

sudo dnf install gcc gcc-c++ make cmake

Arch:

sudo pacman -S base-devel cmake

macOS:

xcode-select --install     # Apple's compiler, once
brew install cmake

macOS builds are untested

Ryokan's automated builds and tests run on Linux only, so a native macOS build may work but nothing checks it. On a Mac, including Apple Silicon, the supported way to run Ryokan is the Docker image. Docker Desktop, OrbStack, and Colima run its arm64 build natively, without emulation.

Then, on any of them:

cargo install cargo-nextest --locked

items.title: Clone and run
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/johnthreekay/Ryokan.git
cd Ryokan
cargo run                # http://localhost:8978; creates data/ryokan.db on first run

The first build takes a while. Rebuilds after that are quick.

items.title: Run it as a service
items.text:
Build a release binary with cargo build --release. A service needs two folders:

  • The install folder, as the working directory. Ryokan loads its stylesheets and scripts from the static folder in the directory it starts in. Started anywhere else, pages load without styling. Either run it from the repository checkout, or copy target/release/ryokan and the static folder side by side, for example to /opt/ryokan/ryokan and /opt/ryokan/static.
  • The data folder, for the database, the encryption key, the caches, and backups. By default it is data inside the working directory. Set RYOKAN_DATA_DIR to keep it apart from the install, and create it owned by the user Ryokan runs as:
sudo useradd --system --home-dir /var/lib/ryokan --shell /usr/sbin/nologin ryokan
sudo install -d -o ryokan -g ryokan /var/lib/ryokan

Any init system works, since all it needs is a working directory and one environment variable. The examples below are for Linux. On macOS, use the Docker image instead.

systemd, as /etc/systemd/system/ryokan.service:

[Unit]
Description=Ryokan
After=network-online.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
User=ryokan
Group=ryokan
WorkingDirectory=/opt/ryokan
Environment=RYOKAN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/ryokan
Environment=RUST_LOG=ryokan=info
ExecStart=/opt/ryokan/ryokan
Restart=on-failure

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

OpenRC, as /etc/init.d/ryokan:

#!/sbin/openrc-run
description="Ryokan"
command="/opt/ryokan/ryokan"
command_user="ryokan:ryokan"
command_background=true
pidfile="/run/${RC_SVCNAME}.pid"
directory="/opt/ryokan"
export RYOKAN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/ryokan
export RUST_LOG=ryokan=info

depend() {
    need net
}

runit, as an executable /etc/sv/ryokan/run:

#!/bin/sh
exec 2>&1
cd /opt/ryokan || exit 1
export RYOKAN_DATA_DIR=/var/lib/ryokan
export RUST_LOG=ryokan=info
exec chpst -u ryokan:ryokan ./ryokan

RUST_LOG=ryokan=info keeps the console log at the level the Docker image uses. Without it, Ryokan logs every request at debug level. This OpenRC example discards console output, and System → Logs keeps Ryokan's log either way.

To move an existing install's data, stop Ryokan and copy everything from the old data folder into the new one, including the hidden .ryokan-key file. Then set RYOKAN_DATA_DIR and start it. Without the copy, Ryokan starts with an empty library. Without the key file, linked AniList and MyAnimeList accounts have to be linked again.

items.title: Tests and lints
items.text:
cargo t                                                                  # the test suite
cargo fmt --all -- --check                                               # formatting (CI runs this first)
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features test-support -- -D warnings   # lints, the way CI runs them

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• Configuration: the Settings tabs.
  • Download clients: per-client setup notes.
  • Docker reference: the environment variable table; the RYOKAN_* variables work the same way when running from source.

Last updated: 2026-10-03.

items.title: Docker installation
items.text:
The Ryokan image is ghcr.io/johnthreekay/ryokan:latest, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64.

This page covers the Ryokan container on its own. For Ryokan together with a media server and a download client, follow the Quick start.

items.title: Quick install
items.text:
Save this as docker-compose.yml:

services:
  ryokan:
    image: ghcr.io/johnthreekay/ryokan:latest
    container_name: ryokan
    ports:
      - "8978:8978"
    volumes:
      - ryokan-data:/data
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=Etc/UTC
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  ryokan-data:

Then run:

docker compose up -d

Open http://localhost:8978 and create your account.

items.title: Recommended install (with a media folder)
items.text:
The quick install lets you search and grab, but Ryokan cannot place finished downloads in your library until it can see both. Add one mount, for a folder that holds your downloads and your library:

services:
  ryokan:
    image: ghcr.io/johnthreekay/ryokan:latest
    container_name: ryokan
    ports:
      - "8978:8978"
    volumes:
      - ryokan-data:/data
      - /srv/media:/srv/media              # downloads and library
    environment:
      - PUID=1000
      - PGID=1000
      - TZ=America/Chicago
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  ryokan-data:

Here /srv/media holds two folders, /srv/media/downloads and /srv/media/anime. Use your own folder in place of /srv/media on both sides of the mount.

  • Enter /srv/media/anime as the Media Root Path, during first-run setup or later under Settings → General.
  • Mount the same folder at the same path in your download client, and have the client save into /srv/media/downloads. Ryokan looks for a finished file at exactly the path the client reports.

Keep downloads and the library in one mount like this. A hardlink only works inside a single mount, and with hardlinks an imported episode takes no extra space while the torrent keeps seeding. With two separate mounts Ryokan has to copy each file instead. See Volume layout.

items.title: PUID and PGID
items.text:
environment:
  - PUID=1000
  - PGID=1000

Ryokan runs as this user and group inside the container. Set them to the user that owns your media, so the files Ryokan writes have the same owner as the rest of your library. To find the values, run id -u and id -g as that user. On most systems both are 1000.

Other containers that follow the linuxserver.io convention use the same two variables. Give them the same values.

Ryokan does not change the owner of your media

On start, the container takes ownership of its own data folder (/data) and nothing else. Your downloads and library folders must already be writable by the user you set here.

items.title: First-run setup
items.text:
The first time you open Ryokan it asks you to create an account. After that the setup page is closed.

If you forget the password, see Reset auth.

items.title: Updating
items.text:
docker compose pull
docker compose up -d

Your data is in the volume and is kept. The database is upgraded automatically on start. See Docker reference → Updating for one command to avoid.

items.title: Where next
items.text:
• Configuration: the Settings tabs.
  • Download clients: setup notes for each client.
  • External accounts: link AniList or MAL.
  • Docker reference: environment variables, reverse proxies and other details.
  • Build from source: run Ryokan without Docker.

Last updated: 2026-11-18.

items.title: Importing an existing library
items.text: If you already have anime on disk, Ryokan can take it over without downloading anything again. System → Import Library scans a folder, matches each show against AniList, shows you what it would do, and then places the files in your media root.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• Set a media root under Settings → General. The wizard does not start without one.
  • Choose a folder outside the media root. Ryokan will not scan its own media root.
  • In Docker, mount the folder into the container and type the path as the container sees it, such as /library.

items.title: Scanning
items.text:
The start form asks for:

  • Folder to scan: a full path. Subfolders are included, up to eight levels deep.
  • How files reach the media root:
    • Hardlink (recommended): the original stays where it is and no extra space is used. This only works when both folders are on the same filesystem. If they are not, the preview warns you and the files are copied.
    • Copy: uses twice the space.
    • Move: removes the files from the source folder.
  • Follow symlinks: off by default.
  • Include hidden files and folders: off by default.

Only video files are imported (.mkv, .mp4, .avi, .wmv, .webm, .m4v, .ts), along with .strm files (see the FAQ).

Each show needs one AniList lookup, and AniList allows about thirty a minute, so a library with hundreds of shows takes a few minutes to scan. You can leave the page. System → Import Library lists recent scans, and a finished preview is kept for two hours after you last used it.

items.title: Reading the preview
items.text:
The preview has one card per series:

  • New series (green): found on AniList and not in your library. Importing adds it.
  • Already in library (blue): matches a series you already have.
  • No match (gray): AniList found nothing for the name Ryokan read. Search with a different title, or skip it.
  • Skipped: you excluded the series.

Two badges are worth checking:

  • Check this match: the AniList title looks different from the name Ryokan read.
  • Also matched by ...: two folders matched the same series. Both are imported into it.

items.title: The file table
items.text:
Each row shows a file, its episode number, its quality, where it would go, and what the import would do with it:

Action Meaning Import You do not have this episode. Replace You have it at a lower quality. The import replaces your file. Already have You have it at the same or better quality. Nothing happens. Downloading A download for this episode is in progress. Pinned Your existing file has a manual quality override and is never replaced. No episode number Ryokan could not read an episode number. The file is not imported. Excluded You unticked it. Already on disk A different file with the same name is already at the destination. It is left alone. Duplicate name Another file in this import has the same destination name. Only the first is written. Special An OVA or special belonging to a TV series. It goes into the series' Specials folder and is not counted as an episode.

Files keep their original names. They are placed in <media root>/<series folder>/<season folder>/.

items.title: How Ryokan reads names
items.text:
Series name. Taken from the file name: [SubsPlease] Sousou no Frieren - 05 (1080p).mkv is Sousou no Frieren. If the file name has no title, as in 01.mkv or S01E05.mkv, Ryokan uses the folder above it, skipping folders like Season 01 and Specials. The card then says name from folder.

Episode number. Read the same way as everywhere else in Ryokan. A file holding several episodes, such as Title - 05-06.mkv, is recorded for each of them.

Season. Read from S02E01, from a marker in the title (S2, Season 2, 2nd Season, II), or from a Season 3 folder. A year in the name, as in Hunter x Hunter (2011), helps pick the right remake.

AniList lists each season as a separate entry, so each season becomes its own series in Ryokan with episodes numbered from 1. This affects the preview in a few ways:

  • A later season gets its own card.
  • Episode numbers can change. If one AniList entry covers what your library calls seasons 1 and 2, S02E05 becomes E17 of that entry, with a was E05 note.
  • One season folder can split into two cards, where AniList lists the two halves of a season separately.
  • A folder numbered straight through, like Jujutsu Kaisen - 55.mkv, is split across the seasons. That file becomes JUJUTSU KAISEN Season 3 E08, with a was E55 note.

Ryokan only does this renumbering for matches it made itself. If you pick a match by hand, the files keep the numbers in their names.

items.title: Correcting a match
items.text:
• Change match: shows the other candidates, each with a Use button. Type in the search box to look for any other title.
  • None of these: removes the match.
  • Skip excludes the whole series. Include brings it back.
  • The checkbox on each row includes or excludes that file. All and None set every row.

Files with no series name in the file name or in any folder above them are listed at the bottom under Files with no series hint. Rename them, or move them into a folder named after the show, and scan again.

items.title: Importing
items.text:
The bar at the bottom shows how many files will be written. Click Import and confirm. The import runs in the background and the page shows its progress. You can leave and come back through System → Import Library.

What the import does:

  • New series are added the way Add Series adds them. They are set to monitor future episodes only, so importing does not start downloads for episodes you are missing. You can change that on the series page.
  • Series already in your library keep their monitoring and folder.
  • Replaced files go to the recycle bin if you have one, and are deleted otherwise.
  • Each imported episode gets a quality tag, and NFO files and artwork are written for Jellyfin.

Cancel import stops after the current file. Files already imported stay imported.

When it finishes, a report lists each series with the number of files imported, replaced and skipped, and any errors.

items.title: Running it again
items.text: You can scan the same folder again. Episodes that were imported show as Already have, and only files you excluded or added since are new.

items.title: Limits
items.text:
• Only one import runs at a time.
  • Files without an episode number are never imported. Rename them so the number can be read.
  • Files are not renamed to your naming templates.
  • The quality in the preview is read from the file name. After the import, Ryokan inspects the file itself, so the quality on the series page can be more specific.

items.title: Quick start
items.text: This guide takes you from a bare Linux server to a full installation of Ryokan and its connectors.

items.title: 1. Install Docker
items.text:
Skip this step if you already have Docker + Docker Compose.

Debian-basedFedora and RHEL-basedArch-basedopenSUSEUnraid, Synology, TrueNAS 
curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh

curl -fsSL https://get.docker.com | sudo sh
sudo systemctl enable --now docker

sudo pacman -S docker docker-compose
sudo systemctl enable --now docker

sudo zypper install docker docker-compose
sudo systemctl enable --now docker

Docker is already part of the system. On Synology, install Container Manager from the Package Center. On Unraid, install the Compose Manager plugin from Community Applications.

Use a folder on your storage pool for the two folders in step 2, for example /mnt/user/media on Unraid or /volume1/media on Synology.

Then let your own user run Docker without sudo:

sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

You'll have to log out and log back in for that to take effect. Check that it works:

docker run --rm hello-world

It should print "Hello from Docker!" along with the steps it took to generate the message.

items.title: 2. Choose your stack
items.text:
The defaults are a good start if you have no preference. You can always come back and change them later.

Download clientPick one or more. qBittorrentRecommended. Deluge Transmission rTorrentComes with the ruTorrent web UI. SABnzbdUsenet. Needs a Usenet provider and indexer. Media serverAllows you to stream your library to other devices. JellyfinRecommended. Free and open source. EmbySome features need Emby Premiere. PlexNeeds a Plex account. NoneYou already have one, or don't want one. RequestsA page where you or your friends/family request anime. None SeerrSends requests to Ryokan. Folders and user Media folderHolds your downloads and your library. Use a full path. Settings folderEach app keeps its settings in a folder under this one. User IDid -u prints yours. Group IDid -g prints yours. Time zoneSuch as America/Chicago. More options: file handling, indexers, VPN, HTTPS, host check File operation modeHow a finished download gets into your library. HardlinkRecommended. No extra disk space, and torrents keep seeding. CopyTorrents keep seeding. Each episode takes its space twice. MoveNo extra disk space. Torrents stop seeding. Indexer managerLets Ryokan search trackers and Usenet indexers besides Nyaa, which is built in. NoneNyaa only. ProwlarrTorrents and Usenet. The usual choice. JackettTorrents only. VPNSends your torrent clients through a VPN with Gluetun. You need a VPN subscription. NoneTorrents use your own connection. GluetunProtonVPN, Mullvad, PIA, NordVPN and others. Reverse proxyPuts Ryokan on your own domain with HTTPS. You need a domain. NoneReach Ryokan by address and port. CaddyGets certificates on its own. The easy one. TraefikConfigured with labels. nginxYou write the config and bring the certificates. Cloudflare TunnelNo open ports on your router. Host checkRyokan's pages then only answer to an IP address, localhost, or the names you list. See Host check. Turn on the host checkOff by default. Names you open Ryokan bySeparate them with spaces. Your stack RyokanqBittorrentJellyfin

Already running one of these?

Pick None for the media server if you have one, or untick the download client and remove it from the file in step 3. Your existing media server has to be able to read /srv/media/anime, and your existing download client has to save into /srv/media/downloads.

items.title: 3. Create the folders and start the stack
items.text:
Create the folders the stack uses, owned by the user from step 2:

Copy commands

sudo mkdir -p \
  /srv/media/downloads \
  /srv/media/anime \
  /srv/docker/ryokan \
  /srv/docker/qbittorrent \
  /srv/docker/jellyfin
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 \
  /srv/media/downloads \
  /srv/media/anime \
  /srv/docker/ryokan \
  /srv/docker/qbittorrent \
  /srv/docker/jellyfin

Next, make a folder for the stack itself, for example /srv/stack, and save this in it as docker-compose.yml:

Copy file

Loading…

rTorrent: set a password before the first start. Without these two files, the ruTorrent page and the address Ryokan uses are open to anyone on your network. Put your own password in place of REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-PASSWORD:

sudo mkdir -p /srv/docker/rutorrent/passwd
docker run --rm httpd:2.4-alpine htpasswd -Bbn admin "REPLACE-WITH-YOUR-PASSWORD" \
  | sudo tee /srv/docker/rutorrent/passwd/rutorrent.htpasswd > /dev/null
sudo cp /srv/docker/rutorrent/passwd/rutorrent.htpasswd /srv/docker/rutorrent/passwd/rpc.htpasswd
sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /srv/docker/rutorrent/passwd

The username is admin.

Plex: add a claim token before the first start. Plex only lets you set up a new server from the same machine, or with a claim token. Get one at plex.tv/claim, paste it into PLEX_CLAIM in the file, and start the stack within four minutes.

VPN: add your provider's details before the first start. In the gluetun part of the file, set VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER and the keys or login your provider gave you. The Gluetun wiki lists what each provider needs. If they are wrong, your torrent clients have no connection at all.

Caddy: put your domain in the file. Replace ryokan.example.com in the caddy part of the file with your own name, and point that name at this server.

Traefik: put your email and domain in the file. Replace you@example.com in the traefik part of the file. Then add the three labels from the comment under it to the ryokan service, with your own name in place of ryokan.example.com.

nginx: write the config before the first start. The comment in the nginx part of the file has a config to start from. Save it as /srv/docker/nginx/conf.d/ryokan.conf, and put your certificate files in /srv/docker/nginx/certs.

Cloudflare Tunnel: paste your tunnel token into the file. Create a tunnel in Cloudflare Zero Trust under Networks → Tunnels, and paste its token into TUNNEL_TOKEN. In the tunnel's settings, add a public hostname that points at http://ryokan:8978.

Start the stack from the folder that holds the file:

docker compose up -d

The first start downloads every app, which can take a few minutes. docker compose ps should then list each one as running.

The addresses below use localhost. If the server is another machine, use its name or IP address in place of localhost.

items.title: 4. Set up your download client
items.text: Each client needs to save into /srv/media/downloads. Ryokan can only hardlink a finished file when the client saved it there.That is where Ryokan picks finished files up from.

items.title: qBittorrent
items.text:
1. qBittorrent prints a temporary password to its log the first time it starts. Find it with:

    docker compose logs qbittorrent | grep -i "temporary password"

  2. Open http://localhost:8080 and log in as admin with your temp password.

  3. Go to Tools → Options → Web UI and set your own password under Authentication.
  4. Go to Tools → Options → Downloads and set Default Save Path to /srv/media/downloads.
  5. Click Save.

items.title: Deluge
items.text:
1. Open http://localhost:8112 and log in with the default password deluge. Change it when Deluge asks.
  2. Go to Preferences → Downloads and set Download to to /srv/media/downloads.
  3. Go to Preferences → Network. Under Incoming Port, untick Use Random Port and set the port to 6881. This is the port the stack opens for Deluge.
  4. Click Apply.

items.title: Transmission
items.text:
1. Open http://localhost:9091. The stack runs Transmission without a login.
  2. Open the preferences and go to Torrents. Set Download to to /srv/media/downloads.
  3. Turn on Use temporary folder and set it to /srv/media/downloads/incomplete.

items.title: rTorrent
items.text:
rTorrent's image saves to its own folder, so its config file needs two changes. Open /srv/docker/rutorrent/rtorrent/.rtorrent.rc in an editor.

  1. Add this line:

    directory.default.set = /srv/media/downloads/temp

  2. Change the line that starts with method.insert = d.get_finished_dir to:

    method.insert = d.get_finished_dir, simple, "cat=/srv/media/downloads/complete/,$d.custom1="

  3. Restart it:

    docker compose restart rutorrent

The ruTorrent page is at http://localhost:8082. Log in as admin with the password from step 3.

items.title: SABnzbd
items.text:
1. Open http://localhost:8081 and go through the setup wizard. This is where you enter your Usenet provider.
  2. Go to Config → Folders. Set Temporary Download Folder to /srv/media/downloads/incomplete and Completed Download Folder to /srv/media/downloads/complete.
  3. Go to Config → Special and add sabnzbd to host_whitelist. Save, and restart SABnzbd. Until you do, SABnzbd answers Ryokan with "Access denied".
  4. Go to Config → General → Security and copy the API Key. Use the full API key, not the NZB key. You need it in step 7.

items.title: 5. Set up your media server
items.text:
You picked no media server, so there is nothing to do here. If you run one somewhere else, give it a library for shows that points at /srv/media/anime.

Open http://localhost:8096 and go through Jellyfin's setup wizard.

  1. Create an admin account. It is separate from Ryokan's.
  2. Add a library with the content type Shows, and give it the folder /srv/media/anime.
  3. Accept the defaults for everything else.

Then make a key for Ryokan. Go to Dashboard → API Keys, click +, and name it "Ryokan". Copy the key. You need it in the next step.

Open http://localhost:8096 and go through Emby's setup wizard.

  1. Create an admin account. It is separate from Ryokan's.
  2. Add a library with the content type TV shows, and give it the folder /srv/media/anime.
  3. Accept the defaults for everything else.

Then make a key for Ryokan. Open Settings (the gear), go to Advanced → API Keys, click New API Key, and name it "Ryokan". Copy the key. You need it in the next step.

Open http://localhost:32400/web and sign in with your Plex account.

  1. Give the server a name.
  2. Add a library of the type TV Shows, and give it the folder /srv/media/anime.

Then find your token for Ryokan. Once the library has something in it, open any episode, click ⋯ → Get Info → View XML, and look at the address of the page that opens. It ends in X-Plex-Token=. The value after it is the token. Until then, leave the media server fields in the next step empty and add them later.

The library stays empty until Ryokan imports its first episode.

items.title: 6. First login to Ryokan
items.text:
Open http://localhost:8978. Ryokan asks you to create an account. Choose a username and a password of 8 to 72 characters. Ryokan has a single user, and this is it.

Next it asks where finished episodes should go:

Field Value Media Root Path /srv/media/anime File operation mode Hardlink

The media server fields on the same page are optional, but filling them in means new episodes show up in Jellyfin straight away:

Field Value Type Jellyfin URL http://jellyfin:8096 API Key The key you made in step 5

The media server fields on the same page are optional, but filling them in means new episodes show up in Emby straight away:

Field Value Type Emby URL http://emby:8096 API Key The key you made in step 5

The media server fields on the same page are optional, but filling them in means new episodes show up in Plex straight away:

Field Value Type Plex URL http://plex:32400 API Key Your token from step 5

Click Save and continue.

You can change any of this later under Settings → General and Settings → Connections. If you click Skip for now instead, Ryokan does not import finished downloads until you fill it in there.

items.title: 7. Add your download client to Ryokan
items.text:
In Ryokan, go to Settings → Download Clients → Add download client. Pick the client's kind, give it any name, and fill in the rest:

qBittorrent

Field Value URL http://qbittorrent:8080 Username admin Password The password you set in step 4 Category anime Download path Leave empty

Deluge

Field Value URL http://deluge:8112 Password The password you set in step 4 Category anime Download path Leave empty

Transmission

Field Value URL http://transmission:9091 Username and password Leave empty Category anime Download path Leave empty

rTorrent

Field Value URL http://rutorrent:8000/RPC2 Username admin Password The password you set in step 3 Category anime Download path Leave empty

SABnzbd

Field Value URL http://sabnzbd:8080 API Key The key you copied in step 4 Category anime Download path Leave empty

Click Test connection. It should say Connected, with a version number. If it does not, see Download clients. Then save.

The first torrent client you add becomes the default for torrents, and the first Usenet client the default for Usenet.

If the client is not part of this stack

The addresses above are names that only work between the apps in this stack. For a client running anywhere else, use the address you would type in a browser, for example http://192.168.1.100:8080.

items.title: 8. Add a show and watch it land
items.text:
On the library page, click + Add Series, type a title, and pick the show from the results.

On the series page, each episode has two buttons. Interactive search lists the available releases, best first, each with a Grab button. Auto search grabs the best one for you. Search Monitored Episodes at the top does the same for every monitored episode.

When the download finishes:

  1. Ryokan places the file in /srv/media/anime, under <show name>/Season 01/. The file is hardlinked, so it takes no extra space and the client keeps seeding.The file is copied, so the client keeps seeding its own copy.The file is moved out of the downloads folder, and Ryokan removes the finished download from the client.
  2. The media server shows the episode straight away if you connected it in step 6. Otherwise it appears after the server's next library scan.

That is a working install. The sections below are for the extras you picked, and for things you can add later.

items.title: Connect Seerr
items.text:
Seerr talks to Ryokan the way it would talk to Sonarr and Radarr. Ryokan plays both parts.

In Ryokan, go to Settings → Connections. Under both Seerr sections, turn on Enable Sonarr API and Enable Radarr API, click Generate beside each API Key, and save. Both are off, with no key, on a new install.

In Seerr, open http://localhost:5055 and go through its setup. When it asks for your media server, the hostname is jellyfin and the port is 8096.When it asks for your media server, the hostname is emby and the port is 8096. When it asks for services, add both of these:

Field Sonarr server (series) Radarr server (films) Hostname ryokan ryokan Port 8978 8978 Use SSL Off Off API Key The Sonarr key from Ryokan The Radarr key from Ryokan URL Base Leave empty /radarr Quality Profile Default Default Root Folder /srv/media/anime /srv/media/anime

Click Test on each before saving. The profile and folder lists fill in once the test passes.

items.title: VPN port forwarding
items.text:
Check first that the VPN is up:

docker compose logs gluetun | tail -n 20

Your torrent clients now download through the VPN, but other peers cannot connect to you until a port is forwarded. Downloads still work without one. Uploads are slow, and private trackers mark you as unconnectable.

Port forwarding needs a provider that offers it. ProtonVPN, PIA, PrivateVPN and AirVPN do. Mullvad and NordVPN do not. If yours does not, remove the two VPN_PORT_FORWARDING lines from the file and skip this section.

First, find the port Gluetun was given:

docker exec gluetun cat /tmp/gluetun/forwarded_port

An empty answer means no port yet. Look in the Gluetun log for the reason.

Then enter that port in your torrent client:

  • qBittorrent: under Tools → Options → Connection, set Port used for incoming connections to the port and untick Use UPnP / NAT-PMP port forwarding. Under Advanced, set Network Interface to tun0.
  • Deluge: under Preferences → Network, set Incoming Port to the port, set Interface to tun0, and turn off UPnP and NAT-PMP.
  • Transmission: in the preferences under Network, set Listening port to the port and untick Use UPnP or NAT-PMP port forwarding.
  • rTorrent: in /srv/docker/rutorrent/rtorrent/.rtorrent.rc, set network.port_range.set to the port twice with a dash between, such as 51234-51234, and set network.port_random.set = no. Then restart it.

Some providers change the port when the VPN reconnects. If uploads stop, read the port again and update the client.

SABnzbd stays outside the VPN. Usenet is an encrypted connection to your provider, with no peers.

items.title: Reverse proxy
items.text:
Once Ryokan opens on your domain over HTTPS, add this to the environment part of the ryokan service in the file and run docker compose up -d again:

RYOKAN_TRUSTED_PROXY: "1"

Ryokan then reads the visitor's real address from the proxy, and marks the login cookie as secure. Only set it behind a proxy. See Docker reference.

The host check is on, so your domain has to be in the list of names in step 2. Without it, every page opened through the proxy answers with a "421" error.

items.title: Add an indexer (optional)
items.text:
Nyaa is built in, so Ryokan can search for anime without a separate indexer.

If you already run Prowlarr or Jackett, go to Settings → Indexers → Add indexer in Ryokan. Paste the indexer's URL, which ends in /api, and its API key, give it a name, and click Test. To run one as part of this stack, pick it under More options in step 2.

items.title: Add indexers with Prowlarr
items.text:
Nyaa is built in, so Ryokan already searches it. Prowlarr adds other trackers and Usenet indexers.

In Prowlarr, open http://localhost:9696 and create a login when it asks.

  1. Go to Indexers → Add Indexer and add the ones you use.
  2. Go to Settings → General and copy the API Key.

In Ryokan, go to Settings → Indexers → Add indexer, once for each indexer in Prowlarr:

Field Value Name Anything, such as the indexer's name Kind torznab for a torrent indexer, newznab for a Usenet one URL http://prowlarr:9696/1/api API Key The key from Prowlarr

The 1 in the URL is the indexer's number in Prowlarr. To find it, click the indexer in Prowlarr's list. Its Torznab Url ends in a number and /api.

Click Test, then save.

items.title: Add indexers with Jackett
items.text:
Nyaa is built in, so Ryokan already searches it. Jackett adds other trackers.

In Jackett, open http://localhost:9117.

  1. Click Add indexer and add the ones you use.
  2. Copy the API Key from the top right of the page.

In Ryokan, go to Settings → Indexers → Add indexer, once for each indexer in Jackett:

Field Value Name Anything, such as the indexer's name Kind torznab URL http://jackett:9117/api/v2.0/indexers/NAME/results/torznab/api API Key The key from Jackett

Put the indexer's own name in place of NAME. To find it, click Copy Torznab Feed beside the indexer in Jackett and look at the address it copies.

Click Test, then save.

items.title: Link AniList or MAL (optional)
items.text: To have Ryokan add shows when you mark them as watching on AniList or MAL, see External accounts. Shows you added by hand are not affected.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text:
• The media server cannot read the files. Ryokan and the media server are then running as different users. Give every app the same user and group ID in step 2, and run the chown command from step 3 again. See PUID and PGID.
  • An app keeps restarting. docker compose logs <name> shows why. The usual cause is a settings folder that was not created in step 3.
  • Troubleshooting covers the rest.

items.title: What next?
items.text:
• Configuration: every Settings tab.
  • Importing an existing library: bring in anime you already have without downloading it again.
  • How releases are scored: why Ryokan picks the release it picks.

Last updated: 2026-11-18.

items.title: How releases are scored
items.text:
Ryokan gives every release it finds a score and grabs the one with the highest. The score is a sum of parts.

To see the parts for a release, open a series page, click Interactive search on an episode, and expand the score next to the release. The names in the tables below are the ones shown there.

items.title: Release signals
items.text:
These apply to every search.

Part Points Seeders +30 over 100, +25 over 50, +20 over 10, +10 for any, -10 for none Preferred Group +140 for the first group on your preferred list, 20 less for each place further down Non-Preferred Group -15 for a group that is not on your list No Group Tag -10 for a release that names no group, when you have a preferred list Preferred Resolution +20 when the release is the resolution you prefer Batch Release +15 Compact Batch +10 more for a batch under 25 GiB Trusted Uploader +10 for a Nyaa release from a trusted uploader Encoding / Source Quality +5 for 10-bit, x265, HEVC, or BluRay in the title Dub / Dual Audio -15 for a dub or dual-audio release when you prefer subs, +15 when you prefer dubs Downloads +15 over 10,000, +10 over 5,000, +5 over 1,000

items.title: Fit for the episode
items.text:
Automatic search adds these. They measure how well the release matches the series and episode being searched for, so that a popular release for the wrong show or episode does not win.

Part Points Title Alias Match up to +40, by how much of the series title, or one of its other names, the release title contains Title Match Confidence 0 for an exact title, -25 for a partial one, and another -10 when the match came through an alternate title or a related series Season Mismatch -100 when the release names a different season Episode Number Match +40 when the release covers the episode Wrong Episode Number -1000 for a release found through a related series that names a different episode Unparseable Episode Number -500 for such a release with no episode number Ryokan can read Single-Episode Target +10 for a single-episode release when one episode is wanted Batch Penalty -20 for a batch when one episode is wanted, -5 for a batch when the whole title is one episode (a movie or an OVA) Movie / Special / OVA +8 when the title is one episode and the release says movie, special, or OVA Preferred Group (auto) +180 for the first group on your preferred list and 30 less per place, -40 for a group not on the list, -15 for no group. Only when you have a list Source / Resolution Fit See below Finished Series BD Bonus +35 for a BluRay release of a finished series when Finished series is set to prefer BD

Source / Resolution Fit is made up of:
