Resolution Source At or above what you prefer +25 +15 Exactly what you prefer +15 more +10 more Below what you prefer -10, and -10 more per step -5, and -5 more per step At or above the cutoff +10 +5 Cannot be read -10 -5

When you prefer BluRay, a BDMV adds 7 and a remux adds 5. A release where neither resolution nor source can be read gets -5.

The preferred resolution and source, the cutoffs, and the finished-series rule are set under Settings → Quality & Releases (Configuration).

items.title: Custom Formats and SeaDex
items.text:
Custom Format scores are added on top. Every format that matches a release contributes its score. See Custom Formats.

Minimum Score on the Custom Formats tab removes releases below that score from automatic searches. Interactive search still shows them.

A release that SeaDex lists as best gets +10,000, which beats everything else combined. Turn it on with the SeaDex switch under Quality & Releases or with the SeaDex Best Custom Format. If both are on, the bonus is still only counted once.

Releases on the blocklist (Downloads → Blocklist) are never scored.

items.title: Replacing a file you already have
items.text:
Ryokan replaces an episode you already have when a release is better in one of three ways. It checks them in this order.

Quality. A higher source or resolution, while the file is below your cutoff. Once the file meets the cutoff, quality alone does not replace it.

Revision. A v2, PROPER or REPACK of the same release from the same group. This replaces the file even if it already meets the cutoff, because a v2 is a fix. Through RSS, this only happens while the file is less than a week old. A v2 from a different group is ignored.

Custom Format score. A release of the same quality with a higher Custom Format score, until the file's score reaches Upgrade Until Custom Format Score. The new release has to score higher by at least the Minimum Custom Format Score Increment. The default cutoff of 0 turns this off for any file scoring 0 or more. This also happens only through RSS, and only for files Ryokan grabbed itself.

The daily upgrade search only looks at files below the quality cutoff. Revision and score upgrades for files that already meet it come through RSS.

Propers and Repacks under Quality & Releases controls how revisions are treated: Prefer and upgrade (the default), Prefer, do not upgrade, or Do not prefer.

To stop a series' files from being replaced, turn off Upgrades on its series page. Ryokan then only grabs episodes you do not have. Searching a single episode yourself, or picking a release in interactive search, still replaces the file.

When a release is not taken, the reason is in the RSS log and the automatic search log.

items.title: What automatic search will and will not grab
items.text:
Automatic search and RSS only take a release whose name contains one of the series' titles exactly and names nothing more. A release called "Dr. Stone New World" is not taken for Dr. STONE.

When a search skips releases for this reason, the toast and the log list them. If one of them is right:

  1. Open the series page and expand Advanced search overrides.
  2. Under Alternate titles, add the name that group uses, one per line.

That name is then searched for and treated as an exact match everywhere: automatic search, RSS, the upgrade search and the misgrab check.

Interactive search shows near matches too, since you choose the release yourself.

items.title: Sequels numbered as one long series
items.text: Fansub groups often keep counting across seasons, so "Jujutsu Kaisen - 56" is season 3, episode 9. Ryokan works out how many episodes came before from AniList's list of sequels, and searches under the earlier seasons' names as well. Where AniList is missing a link, it uses anime-relations, a community-maintained list that ships with Ryokan.

items.title: Search tips
items.text:
• The Search page searches Nyaa directly. Use the uploader field to find a specific group's releases. The category menu switches between English-translated releases and all anime, and the filter menu can limit results to trusted uploaders.
  • Add "batch" to a query to find season packs, for example "Jujutsu Kaisen batch 1080p".
  • Interactive search on a series page searches Nyaa, your indexers and your feeds together and ranks the results. Default custom query tokens under Quality & Releases are added to it, and a series can set its own under Advanced search overrides.

items.title: Grabbing a release
items.text:
Click Grab next to a release to send it to your download client. When the download finishes, Ryokan imports it.

A torrent with several files opens the file picker first, so you can leave out samples and extras. Turn the picker off with Interactive file picker under Settings → General.

Closing the picker does not cancel the grab

If you close the picker, the tab or the page without confirming, the release is grabbed a couple of minutes later with the files that were ticked. To cancel, untick everything and then close it.

items.title: System
items.text: The System page shows what Ryokan has been doing: logs, RSS activity, background tasks, backups, and a few other tools. Settings that change how Ryokan behaves are under Settings instead.

items.title: Logs
items.text:
Everything Ryokan does is logged here. When something did not work, this is the first place to look.

  • Category: one per part of Ryokan (Search, Grab, AniList, DownloadClient, PostProcess, and so on).
  • Level: trace, debug, info, warn or error. Ryokan only stores info and above unless you lower RYOKAN_DB_LOG_LEVEL. See Environment variables.
  • Search: matches text in the message and detail columns, so you can look for a release title or file name.
  • Live: shows new entries as they arrive.

Entries are listed newest first, 200 to a page. Filters and the page number are kept in the address bar, so you can reload or share the link. Logs older than about 30 days are deleted.

Troubleshooting covers what to look for in specific cases.

items.title: RSS
items.text:
The history of RSS checks, one row per feed each time it was checked: how many items came back, the newest title, and the error if the check failed.

Use it to see whether Ryokan saw a release you expected it to grab, or whether a feed has stopped working.

Sync RSS Now checks all feeds immediately. The schedule is set under Settings → General → RSS Sync Interval.

items.title: Scheduled Tasks
items.text:
Ryokan's background tasks, such as the watch-list sync, post-processing, the upgrade search, and metadata refresh. Each row shows the schedule, the result of the last run and when it ran, and a Run now button.

If a feature seems stuck, check here whether its task is running and what the last run reported.

items.title: Import Library
items.text: A wizard for anime you already have on disk. See Importing an existing library.

items.title: Backup
items.text:
Create backups, keep them in a folder, and restore from one.

A backup is a .tar.gz containing the database, the encryption key that protects your linked AniList and MyAnimeList accounts, and the cached artwork if you tick that option.

A backup contains your passwords

It holds the encryption key, your account tokens, and every download client password. Store it as you would any secret.

To send a backup to someone for support, tick Sanitize. Passwords, API keys and tokens are blanked, the log is cut to its last 1000 lines, and the encryption key is left out.

  • Download backup builds a backup and downloads it in your browser.
  • Save to backup folder writes one to the folder set under Settings → General and deletes old ones beyond the number you keep. The folder's backups are listed below, each with Download and Delete.
  • Scheduled backups are off by default. Turn them on under Settings → General.

By default the backup folder is /data/backups, on the same volume as the database. Point it at another disk if the backup should survive losing that volume.

items.title: Restoring
items.text:
1. Upload a backup. Ryokan checks it, saves a backup of the current state to the backup folder (auto-pre-restore-<time>.tar.gz), and stages the restore.
  2. Restart Ryokan. In Docker: docker compose restart ryokan. Ryokan does not restart itself.

Until you restart, the tab shows the staged backup and a Cancel restore button. After the restart everyone is signed out.

Things to know:

  • A backup made by a newer version of Ryokan is refused.
  • A sanitized backup restores, but you have to enter passwords and link accounts again.
  • The previous database is kept next to the restored one as ryokan.db.pre-restore-<time>. Delete it once you are happy with the restore.

items.title: Needs Review
items.text:
Episodes where Ryokan was not sure of the source (BluRay or WEB) or the release group. For each one you can accept its guess or set the right value.

Keeping these correct matters for upgrades, since Ryokan compares new releases against the quality it thinks you have. Unusual file names and imported libraries produce most of the entries.

Notifications for these are off by default, because a reclassify run can produce hundreds at once.

items.title: Misgrabs
items.text:
A misgrab is a download whose files clearly belong to a different series than the one it was grabbed for. By default Ryokan removes it from the download client, blocklists the release, notifies you, and searches again.

This tab lists what was caught: the series, the release, some of its file names, and what happened to it.

  • Restore: the release was right after all. Ryokan stops treating it as a misgrab and adds the download back if it was removed.
  • Dismiss: it was a misgrab. The release stays blocklisted and the row is removed. If the download is still in the client, it is removed now.

Downloads whose file names contain no title, like 01.mkv, are never treated as misgrabs. Neither are files that share a word with the series title, so abbreviated fansub names are safe.

To keep misgrabs in the download client until you decide, turn off Remove and blocklist detected misgrabs under Settings → General. They are then listed here and never imported.

items.title: Notifications
items.text:
Where Ryokan sends notifications.

  • Discord: posts to a Discord webhook URL.
  • Webhook: posts JSON to any URL, for ntfy, Apprise, n8n or your own receiver.

For each one, choose which events it receives: Grabbed, Imported, Import failed, Classifier needs review, Indexer down, Download client unreachable, Re-link required. Send test sends a test event.

Verifying webhook signatures

Set a secret and Ryokan signs each request so the receiver can check where it came from.

  • X-Ryokan-Signature is sha256= followed by the HMAC-SHA256 of the body.
  • X-Ryokan-Signature-V2 is t=<timestamp>,sha256=<hex>, computed over <timestamp>.<body>. Check this one and reject old timestamps to guard against replays.

The autobrr webhook is something else: it sends releases to Ryokan, and is set up under Settings → Indexers.

items.title: Things to check first
items.text:
Three places answer most questions:

  • System → Logs. Filter by the category for whatever went wrong: Grab, AutoSearch, Nyaa, DownloadClient, PostProcess, AniList, and so on. See Logs.
  • Test connection on each download client and indexer under Settings.
  • Grab History. Click an episode on its series page. The history lists every release grabbed for it, with its state and time.

items.title: SAB downloads disappear from Ryokan but still download in SAB
items.text:
SABnzbd does not have the category Ryokan is set to use, so it put the download in its default category, where Ryokan does not look.

Click Test connection on the SABnzbd client under Settings → Download Clients. Ryokan creates the category and moves the download into it.

If the test reports SAB rejected category creation: HTTP 403, you gave Ryokan the NZB key. Use the full API key from SABnzbd's Config → General → Security.

items.title: Episode shows "Importing…" forever
items.text:
The download finished but the file has not been placed in your library.

  • Post-processing is off. Turn it on under Settings → General. If it is off on purpose and the row still says "Importing…", reload the page.
  • The import is failing. Check System → Logs, category PostProcess. The usual causes:
    • Ryokan cannot write to the media root
    • the disk is full
    • Ryokan cannot see the download folder at the path the client reports. See Per-client download paths.

After 24 hours with nothing to import, Ryokan marks the download failed and puts the release on the blocklist. The limit is Give up on stuck imports under Settings → General. To try again, fix the cause, remove the release from Downloads → Blocklist, and search again. The download itself stays in the client, so delete it there if you no longer want it.

items.title: Finished downloads stay in the client
items.text:
Ryokan removes a download once it has been imported and has finished seeding. If one is still there:

  • Remove completed downloads is off for that client. Edit the client under Settings → Download Clients.
  • It is still seeding. A torrent is removed only after the client stops it at a ratio or time limit. Set a limit in the client, with pause or stop as the action, not delete. rTorrent needs a ratio group in .rtorrent.rc.
  • You paused it yourself. Those are left alone.
  • The import failed or was partial. Those stay so you can look at them.
  • It only just finished. Ryokan checks every five minutes.

items.title: Ryokan removed a download it decided was the wrong series
items.text:
Ryokan compares the file names in each download with the series it was grabbed for. When they clearly belong to another show, it removes the download, blocklists the release and searches again. System → Misgrabs shows what was caught and the file names it looked at.

If the release was right, click Restore. Ryokan adds it back and does not flag it again.

If one series keeps producing misgrabs, groups probably name it differently from AniList. Add the name they use under Advanced search overrides → Alternate titles on the series page. Ryokan stops searching again automatically after three misgrabs for a series in a day.

To decide each case yourself, turn off Remove and blocklist detected misgrabs under Settings → General.

items.title: Files ending in .ryokan-tmp or .ryokan-new in the library
items.text:
These are left behind when an import is interrupted, for example by a restart while a large file was being copied. Ryokan cleans them up hourly once they are more than two hours old. A newer one may be a copy in progress, so leave it.

A .ryokan-new file is a complete episode that was about to replace an older one. It goes to the recycle bin if you have one. To keep it, rename it in the season folder: remove the leading dot and the .ryokan-new ending.

items.title: Search returns no results
items.text:
Check System → Logs, categories Search and AutoSearch. Common causes:

  • Your quality settings exclude everything on offer. Loosen them under Settings → Quality & Releases, or use Interactive search on the episode to see everything.
  • Minimum Score under Settings → Custom Formats is filtering releases out of automatic searches. Interactive search still shows them.
  • An indexer is down. It simply adds nothing to the results. Run Test on each indexer.

items.title: Auto search saw releases but grabbed none
items.text:
Automatic search only takes a release whose name contains one of the series' titles exactly. When it skips releases that came close, the toast says "looked close but none named the series exactly" and lists some. System → Logs has them all.

If one is right, add that name on the series page under Advanced search overrides → Alternate titles and search again. See What automatic search will and will not grab.

items.title: RSS skipped a release it used to grab
items.text:
Since 2.3.0, RSS is stricter about releases that use a shortened title, such as "Ano Hana", or that tag a first season S01 when the series' titles name no season. System → RSS lists such a release as "No tracked series match".

Add the name the release uses under Advanced search overrides → Alternate titles on the series page. The next sync takes it.

items.title: An adult title finds nothing
items.text:
Nyaa keeps adult releases on sukebei, which Ryokan's built-in search does not cover. You need an indexer that carries them, such as sukebei through Prowlarr or Jackett.

If a search is still empty, run it in Prowlarr or Jackett directly. If it finds releases there, check that the indexer is enabled in Ryokan and passes its test. You can also set the indexer's Categories field yourself under Settings → Indexers.

items.title: AniList keeps returning 429 Too Many Requests
items.text:
AniList limits how many requests it accepts each minute. Open the latest failure in System → Logs. Its detail line looks like this:

[limit=30 remaining=0 reset=1777813117 retry_after=6 ryokan_60s=27]

ryokan_60s is how many requests Ryokan itself made in the last minute.

  • ryokan_60s is low: something else used up the limit. This could be an anilist.co tab open in your browser, a second Ryokan using the same account, or another tool.
  • ryokan_60s is close to 30: Ryokan sent too many. That is a bug, so please report it.
  • no rate-limit headers: the 429 did not come from AniList's rate limit. It may be Cloudflare or a proxy in between.

items.title: AniList per-account cooldown stuck past 60s
items.text:
If syncs keep failing with 429 even though Ryokan is making very few requests, AniList has put your account in a longer cooldown. This can last hours.

  1. Stop any other Ryokan using the same account.
  2. Close any anilist.co tabs.
  3. Do not press Sync now. Ryokan retries less and less often by itself.
  4. Wait. The cooldown ends without you doing anything.

Linking the account again does not help, because linking counts against the same limit.

items.title: Series page shows something out of date
items.text: The page updates download progress every 5 seconds. If something looks wrong, reload the page. If it is still wrong after a reload, open the episode's Grab History, which shows what Ryokan has recorded for it.

items.title: I deleted an episode or series by accident
items.text:
If you have a recycle bin set under Settings → General, open the Library page and click the recycle bin icon in the toolbar. Each deleted episode or series folder has a Restore button.

Restoring a series folder brings back the files but not the library entry. Add the series again and Ryokan finds the files.

Items are deleted for good after 14 days by default. If no recycle bin was set when you deleted, the files are gone.

items.title: Ryokan fails to start with a database error
items.text:
The database file may have been damaged by an earlier crash. To check:

  1. Stop Ryokan: docker compose down ryokan. Do not add -v.
  2. Copy the database somewhere safe: cp /srv/docker/ryokan/ryokan.db /srv/docker/ryokan/ryokan.db.backup. Use your own data folder's path.
  3. Run sqlite3 /srv/docker/ryokan/ryokan.db "PRAGMA integrity_check;".

If it prints anything other than ok, the database is corrupt. Restore a backup, or delete the file and start again from first-run setup.

Last updated: 2026-08-29.

items.title: Wanted
items.text: The Wanted page lists the episodes Ryokan still needs. It has two tabs.

items.title: Missing
items.text: Monitored episodes that have aired and are neither in your library nor downloading, grouped by series. Episodes that have not aired yet are not listed, and neither are series you do not monitor.

items.title: Quality cutoff unmet
items.text: Episodes you have whose quality is below your cutoff (Settings → Quality & Releases), with the quality of the current file. Only series that allow upgrades are listed. The daily upgrade search works through this same list.

items.title: Searching
items.text:
Each row has two buttons:

  • Auto search grabs the best release for every episode listed in the row.
  • Interactive opens a list of releases for you to choose from.

To search several series at once, tick their rows and press Search selected, or press Search all. Both run automatic searches, one series at a time. A toast shows the progress and how many releases were grabbed. A second run cannot start while one is going.

items.title: Interactive search
items.text:
The Search for menu at the top of the window sets what is listed:

  • Episodes 3-11 (the default when a series is missing more than one episode): single-episode releases for all the wanted episodes, sorted by episode. Batches are not shown here.
  • Episode N: releases for that one episode.
  • Batch releases: season packs and complete releases.

Press Grab on the release you want.

Grabbing a batch opens the file picker with only the files for your missing episodes ticked. A twelve-episode pack for two missing episodes downloads two files, unless you tick more.

Closing the picker does not cancel the grab

If you close the picker without confirming, the ticked files are grabbed a couple of minutes later. To cancel, untick everything and then close it.

When a series is missing a large number of episodes, search for a batch. The Episodes search runs a separate query for each of the first twelve wanted episodes only.

items.title: Older gaps
items.text: Ryokan does not search for missing episodes on a schedule. RSS picks up new episodes as they are released, and the upgrade search runs daily. For anything older, search from this page.
